glossary.Steady: Initiative cannot be reduced by Tactics.
glossary.Unwieldy: Initiative cannot be improved by Tactics.
glossary.Deadly: On a Focused Strike: increase AP by -5, and the defender may Parry or Recover only with a Focused roll.
glossary.Unstoppable: Parried only by a Focused roll.
glossary.Cleave: On a Focused Strike: roll one extra Strike die at your modified to-Strike.
glossary.Poison: When the Defender receives a Strike and rolls a Focused Save, it fails; the resulting wound may only be Recovered with a Focused Recover.
glossary.Nimble: Gain +1 Initiative in the first Skirmish of each Battle.
glossary.Drilled: Does not lose Endurance in the first Skirmish of each Battle.
glossary.Destroy Shield: On a Focused Strike: the target loses its Shield attributes for the rest of the Battle.
glossary.Blunder: At Initiative -2 or lower, your to-Strike is set to 6+, before other negative modifiers.
glossary.One Shot: May only be Equipped in the first Skirmish of a Battle. Requires a Tiltyard.
glossary.Parry: While not Fatigued, roll a d6 to attempt to Parry a Strike before the Save. On a 5+, the Strike is Parried.
glossary.Riposte: While not Fatigued, if you Focused a Parry against a Melee Weapon's Strike, you Riposte: your opponent immediately takes a Strike from your melee weapon. You can Riposte a Riposte.
glossary.Recover: While not Fatigued, if a to-Save roll fails, roll a d6: a result of X+ Recovers the retinue.
glossary.Serrated: -2 to Recover against this weapon's Strikes (worsens the defender's Recover roll by 2).
glossary.Tempered: A Focused Save succeeds, regardless of AP.
glossary.Fatigue Token: Each token is -1 to your Strike to a maximum of 6+; and Morale -1 (uncapped). If your modified Morale is ever 7+, your army Routs. Tokens stack.
glossary.Shielded: A stacking -1 penalty to the Strike roll (to a maximum of 6+). Sources: a shield's -1 to Strike.
glossary.Negate Tempered: Ignores Tempered: this weapon's AP can reduce the target's Save past 6+ (to auto-fail), defeating the Tempered floor.
glossary.Negate Riposte: The target's Parry can never Riposte this weapon's Strikes (a natural 6 Parry still cancels the Strike, but no counter-Strike follows).
glossary.Dual Wield: A Strike die that fails to Strike is rerolled once; the reroll can Focused Strike. Dual Wield confers 2H (both hands on weapons — no Shield). You cannot reroll successful Strikes.
glossary.Florentine: Only active while Dual Wielding. Even while Fatigued, a Focused Parry succeeds. This alone does not enable Riposte while Fatigued.
glossary.Immune [keyword]: Cancels that keyword as it applies to you (e.g. Immune Unwieldy, Strain, Destroy Shield).
glossary.AP: Armor Penetration — a weapon's (negative) modifier to the defender's Save roll; the more negative, the harder to save.
glossary.Blocked: -1 Initiative in the first Skirmish (negated by Immune Blocked).
glossary.Strained: -1 Initiative every Skirmish (negated by Immune Strain). Does not gain Endurance in the Empire Phase.
glossary.Seize the Initiative: Won by the roll-off at the start of the Battle — the winner of their last Battle adds +1 to the roll. You become the Attacker and gain +1 Initiative in the first Skirmish. Some Tactics and the Ministry monument also grant it.
glossary.Attacker / Defender: Set by the roll-off. Each Skirmish the Attacker declares equipment first; the Defender then responds.
glossary.Battle: One fight between two players, resolved as a series of Skirmishes until a side is wiped out, Routs, or Falls Back.
glossary.Skirmish: One round of a Battle, run through the numbered Battle steps; a Battle repeats Skirmishes until it ends.
glossary.Casualty: A retinue removed from the field — from an unsaved Strike or a failed Panic or Break check.
glossary.Field: Your retinues in play — front line (up to 10) plus reserve (up to 5). Casualties leave the field at once, lowering its count.
glossary.Endurance: A side's stamina. Each side that fights loses 1 per Skirmish; at 0 it becomes Fatigued.
glossary.Fatigued: A side at 0 Endurance. Each Skirmish its field takes a Break check, then it gains a Fatigue token. Fatigued Armies cannot Parry, Riposte, or Recover
glossary.Break check: Taken by each Fatigued side's field every Skirmish, just before it gains its Fatigue token. Roll Morale (up to 5 dice, modified by Fatigue tokens); failures are casualties, but a Break check never triggers a Panic check. Unbreakable auto-passes.
glossary.Panic check: Taken at most once per Skirmish by a side that suffered more than 5 casualties in that Skirmish, after it Strikes back. Roll Morale (up to 5 dice); Immune Panic auto-passes.
glossary.Morale: How steady a retinue is when tested (lower is steadier; see the retinue table). Break and Panic checks roll it: a D6 per retinue in the field, up to 5 dice, each must meet its modified value; failures are casualties. If the modified value is ever 7+, the army Routs.
glossary.Rout: The army breaks and leaves the Battle (you lose it). Whenever an army's modified Morale value reaches 7 or more, it Routs automatically.
glossary.Fall Back: A controlled retreat that ends the Battle with at least one retinue left — a partial success.
glossary.Strike: A landed hit. Roll a D6, apply modifiers to the roll, and Strike on a result >= the to-Strike number. The target may then Parry, Save, and Recover.
glossary.to-Strike number: The D6 result a retinue needs to Strike (see the retinue table; lower is better). Bonuses add to the roll; penalties and Fatigue tokens subtract.
glossary.Save: The defender's roll to avoid a casualty: roll a D6, add the weapon's AP (a negative) and the shield's Save bonus (a positive); the hit is saved on a result >= the armor value.
glossary.Natural roll: The number on the die before any modifiers. Modifiers never change what counts as 'natural'.
glossary.Initiative: Decides who Strikes first each Skirmish (higher first). Runs -2 to +2 (Ministry can raise the maximum to +3). At -2 or lower you Blunder.
glossary.Tactic: A choice both players make secretly and reveal together each Skirmish; it can shift Initiative, Strike, and Save rolls.
glossary.Dual-equip: Carry two weapons at once (e.g. melee + ranged). Granted by the Tiltyard, which also gives Unwieldy until its mastery removes it.
glossary.Edict: A scoring achievement / win path: reach a Sovereign Standing, complete a Monument, or fulfill a victory condition (Wonder, wealth, Vassalize, Living Saints, Last Standing).
glossary.Monument: A Domain's capstone Pursuit. Completing one scores its Edict and grants a powerful effect.
glossary.Faith X: Gain X Faith: each Faith raises your Public Order track by 1 when resolved.
glossary.Doubt X: Gain X Doubt: each Doubt lowers your Public Order track by 1 when resolved.
glossary.Extort X: Take X from the stated source: the gold goes to you instead of its owner.
glossary.Recoup: Regain the stated cost in gold after paying it.
glossary.Speed: An Army's movement allowance in Territories per Move action. Base Speed value of an army is Speed 2
glossary.Influence: The political currency of voting. Spend it to Support or Oppose Envoys. You gain it each turn from your Era, innate modifiers (trade partners, alliances, war), Pursuits, and Infrastructure.
glossary.Influence X: An automatic +X (or -X) to an Envoy's net Influence from a Pursuit, Infrastructure, or Faction.
glossary.Envoy: The currency of actions: send an Envoy to perform an action during the Envoy Phase. Council Envoys act on the voted Domain; Personal Envoys are sent by Era progression.
glossary.Vote: On each Envoy, every player in clockwise order from the starting player must Support, Oppose, or Abstain.
glossary.Support X: Spend X Influence to increase an Envoy's net Influence.
glossary.Oppose X: Spend X Influence to decrease an Envoy's net Influence.
glossary.Abstain: Decline to spend Influence on a vote.
glossary.Net Influence: The sum of an Envoy's starting Influence (1+ by Standing) and all Support, Oppose, and Influence X. The total sets the outcome: -3 or less Condemned, 0 or less Failed (gain Doubt +1), 1+ passes.
glossary.Endorsed: An Envoy that passes with 3+ net Influence, triggering its endorsed effect (and a Domain's Rising/Established/Sovereign endorsement).
glossary.Condemned: An Envoy whose net Influence is -3 or less: it fails and you resolve that Domain's Condemn effect.
glossary.Council Phase: Before Personal Envoys, all players vote on a Domain (clockwise; Host breaks ties). Each then sends a free Council Envoy of that Domain. Council Envoys auto-Abstain and their net Influence cannot drop below 1.
glossary.Council Envoy: A free Envoy resolved in the Council Phase on the voted Domain; auto-Abstained, net Influence floored at 1.
glossary.Personal Envoy: An Envoy you send in the Envoy Phase to perform an action; count and reach scale with Era.
glossary.Envoy Outcome: How a Sent Envoy resolves, by Net Influence: Condemned (<= -3), Failed (-3 < Net <= 0, gain Doubt 1), Passed (>= 1), Endorsed (>= 3). The per-domain effect at each band is given by ENVOY_OUTCOMES; an action's own endorsed bonus overrides the domain default.
glossary.Charter: Found or upgrade a Settlement (Industry action).
glossary.Muster: Raise retinues into an Army, up to a Settlement's muster limit (Industry/Prowess).
glossary.Pursue: Build a Pursuit, spending its purchase cost and a Settlement ward (Industry).
glossary.Move: Advance an Army up to its Speed in Territories (Prowess).
glossary.Demand Tribute: Coerce gold or concessions from another player (Prowess).
glossary.Diplomacy: Free Envoy actions for forming and ending Treaties and Trade Agreements; resolved before Domain Envoys.
glossary.Treaty: A standing agreement between players (e.g. Trade Agreement, Non-Aggression, Alliance) signed via Diplomacy.
glossary.Alliance: A Treaty binding players to mutual support; Military and Defensive Alliances unlock by Era.
glossary.Vassal: A player subordinated via Vassalization: their chartered settlements return to them, they mirror the Suzerain's Treaties, count as allied to the Suzerain, and cannot perform or be targeted by Diplomacy actions.
glossary.Suzerain: The player who has Vassalized another; the vassal mirrors their Treaties.
glossary.Renown: The shared progress track. Gain 1 per Rest Phase; thresholds raise your Era (Ascension 8, Eminence 18, Zenith 30).
glossary.Domain: One of the four identities — Industry, Prowess, Cunning, Piety — raised by spending Domain points. Values 3/6/10 = Rising/Established/Sovereign Standing.
glossary.Domain Point: Gained 1 per Rest Phase; spend to raise a Domain value by 1.
glossary.Standing: Your tier in a Domain: Untested, Rising (3), Established (6), Sovereign (10). Sets max Influence per vote (1/2/3/4) and unlocks Domain effects.
glossary.Public Order: A track from -5 to 10, adjusted each turn by Faith minus Doubt; its band applies cumulative effects (see the Public Order table).
glossary.Reach: How far a Settlement projects control, in Territories (by tier). Calculated like Range X
glossary.Bandit: Neutral hostile force; Bandit Camps spawn in Outlaw Country and on low Public Order.
glossary.Outlaw Country: Uncontrollable territories in your starting region where Bandit Camps spawn, starting at 3 and expanding if there is no room to place new Bandit Camps.
glossary.Siege: Sieging a Settlement with an Army to capture it; does not increment in Winter.
glossary.Border: Your Settlement's Reach is Range 1 or within Reach of another Player's Reach.
glossary.Province: The collection of Contested Territory and Controlled Territory by your Settlement's Reach.
glossary.Region: A collection of Territories of the same Type.
glossary.Contested: Territory that is within Reach of more than one player's settlement(s). Considered Controlled by all Players that have a Settlement within Reach.
glossary.Controlled: Territory that is within Reach of a single Player's Settlement(s).
glossary.Uncontrolled: Territory that is not within Reach of any Player Settlement.
glossary.Range X: The amount of Territories you must move in order to get from your current position to the specific Territory.
glossary.Reach X: The Range X characteristic which determines what Territories you Control and are in your Province.
glossary.Perform: When you Perform an action, immediately do the description of the action. Pay the action's normal Cost.
glossary.Cost / Pay: Cost to perform an action, usually in Gold or Doubt.
glossary.Fail: An unsuccessful to Hit or to Save.

factions: The Battering Ram
Siege Specialist: You begin the game with a Siege Works (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery). If a player builds a Citadel, you must Siege it as a Personal Win Condition.
The Boundless Steppe
Horsemasters: Begin the game with a Stable which does not occupy a Settlement ward, cost Upkeep, and counts as an activated Mastery Effect which cannot be deactivated.
The Bandit King

Friends in Low Places: You begin the game with a Smuggler's Nook which does not occupy a Settlement ward, nor cost upkeep. You always gain its Mastery Effect, which cannot be deactivated. In addition, you may control one Bandit Camp outside your territory each turn. Every turn a Bandit Camp is generated, you may place it in your Outlaw Country instead.
The Crowned Star
The Monarch: Each Turn, you choose each Council Envoy's Domain. All Envoys you send gain Influence -1.
The Crimson Tide

Sea Lanes: Other players cannot perform Intercept Caravan on you. You begin the game with a Shipyard that does not occupy a Settlement ward, does not cost upkeep, and always has the Mastery Effect, even if you do not have a Water Settlement.
The Entwined Crown

Royal Marriage: Once per game, you may join an Alliance without unanimous consent, or form an Alliance with a player who is not in one. Whoever is in that Alliance gains Faith +1 and +1 Influence per turn.
The Eternal Court

Patient Court: Your influence is never wasted — unspent influence is not discarded in the Rest Phase. Once the Era is Zenith, you have a cap of 5 on influence you spend per envoy, regardless of your Domain Standing.
The Final Word
The Decider: Ignore the Innate Doubt & Influence Modifiers that are triggered for being at War.
The Gilded Crescent
Prosperity For All: Begin the game with an Inn which does not occupy a Settlement ward, cost Upkeep, and counts as an activated Mastery Effect which cannot be deactivated.
The Gilded Path
Silk Road: You begin the game with an Artisan Workshop (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery). However, you cannot refuse a Trade Agreement.
The Hermit Crown

Independent, but Ambitious: You Abstain every Vote on other players' Envoys, and other players must use 2 Influence to affect your Envoys by 1. Gain Influence +1 to all Personal Envoys. You cannot vote on Council Envoys.
The Illuminated Order
Knowledge is Power: For every 3 Pursuits, gain +1 Influence each turn.
The Iron Faith
Fortress of Faith: While Public Order is greater than or equal to 3, Lay Siege actions targeting Settlements you Control have Siege Timer +2.
The Iron Shore

Scavengers: Whether you win or lose a battle, collect the Spoils of War. You may also recoup the cost of the retinues received as Casualties in that Battle. Lastly, whenever you perform the Rrpair action, recoup its cost, even if it only passed.
The Iron Throne
Unimpeachable: Begin the game with a Citadel (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery). You (or your alliance) cannot perform Declare War or Crusade.
The Merchant Republics

Heart of Trade: Begin the game with Stone Roads infrastructure, do not pay Upkeep, and cannot be Razed. In order for any player to be able to trade, they must trade with this player first, unless at War with this player. As soon as another player is eligible, you must attempt to Sign a Trade Agreement once with that player. You may not perform the End Treaty Diplomacy action.
The Sacred Throne
Sacrosanct: Players who declare war on you (and their allies) gain an additional Doubt +1.
The Tunnellers
Tunnellers: You treat mountain territory like grasslands for purposes of movement, and begin the game with a Mine raw material pursuit (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery).
The Undying Flame

Martyrdom: Your armies Morale cannot be modified beyond 6+, but your armies continue to suffer −1 from Fatigue Tokens. Gain Faith +1 for every player you're at War with and every Battle where you lose 20 or more retinues, win or loss.
The Verdant Kingdom

Peaceful & Inventive: You cannot declare war, enter Military Alliances, perform Cunning actions, or build Pursuits that require Prowess or Cunning Standing. In the Income step, gain 100 gold for each Craft Mastery Effect you have active.
The Winter Wolves
Danegeld: Your armies do not pay upkeep in enemy territory when you're at war — the enemy player pays the upkeep instead. Do not gain Speed −1 in Winter.
The Ancient Wilds

Highlander Way: Enemy armies gain Speed −1 in your Province. You ignore all Terrain Speed modifiers and may trade without Dirt Roads. You must accept the first Non-Aggression Pact offered by each player or Alliance. If that player later joins an alliance, this condition is considered satisfied for that alliance.
The Bloodied Cross

Prophets of War: May Crusade at Rising Piety instead of Sovereign Piety, and do not have a cap on how many Crusades you may have active. All players receive Doubt +1 per Crusade you are on. You cannot perform convert actions.
The Blazing Standard

Burning Cross: You begin the game with a Preceptory of the Knight's Templar (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery). If you Declared War via Crusade, that player must take a Panic Check at the beginning of every battle after lines are formed. If during the Prowess Envoy phase you do not have an army with 25 Knight's Templars, you must attempt to send an envoy. If it passes, you must muster an army until it has 25 retinues of Knight's Templar.
The Inner Circle
Palatine: Players who are allied with you gain Influence +1 to their envoys, but you may spend 1 of their Influence each turn, targeting your own envoys if you wish.
The Luminous Court
Arts & Humanities / Hearts & Minds: Cannot pursue Craft Pursuits. Civic Pursuits gain Craft +1. All Civic Pursuits do not cost Upkeep. This Player must accept a Peace Treaty if offered one.
The Grand Compact
Mercantile Pact: If anyone Declares War on you, players with Trade Agreements with you must Declare War back or End Trade Agreement.
The Pale Throne
Inexorable: Your armies always have Unwieldy and cannot gain Immune Unwieldy, but also gain Recover +1, Speed −1, and Immune Panic. Your Public Order cannot exceed 1.
The Sublime Gate
Integrated Arms: You may Muster retinues and equipment from your Trade Partners' Pursuits (and Mastery Effects, if active) for their cost when you perform a muster action.
The Velvet Hand
Friends in High Places: At the beginning of the turn, players gain Faith +1 if they supported an envoy you sent and it was passed. And, if it was endorsed, they Extort 500 gold per Era.
The Ashen Vale
Pestilence: Each bordering player gains Doubt +1, your settlements gain Reach +1, and all retinues gain Poison. You may not pursue an Apothecary, Infirmary, or Hospitaller.
The Broken Banner

The Highest Bidder: You cannot Declare War and cannot be the Target of a Declare War action. However you must sign any Military or Defensive Alliance offered to you by the highest bidding player each turn and must be paid each turn. In order to overturn an existing alliance, the player must pay a higher amount than the prior agreement. You cannot sign or end alliances via a Diplomacy action.
The Forked Tongue

Masters of Duplicity: You may hold any number of treaties simultaneously with any number of players, regardless of contradiction. Your treaties are never automatically canceled or voided by game events. When a situation arises that would normally force a treaty to be canceled, you may choose which obligation to honor, keeping all other treaties intact. Other players may still end their treaties with you via the End Treaty action.
The Hall of Masks
Mimic: At the beginning of every player's turn, pick another player's Faction. You gain that Faction for this turn. Next turn, you cannot select that Faction.
The Smoldering Crown

Reckless: Gain Influence +2 to all Cunning Envoys when targeting a Player with PO > 0. You begin the game with a Secret Cellar (no ward, no upkeep, always active Mastery). Cannot be in an alliance. Cannot perform Diplomacy actions. If you Send a Prowess envoy, it cannot fail — if condemned, it passes.
The Squatters' Crown

Occupy: You start the game with an additional army. All must begin the game placed inside your settlements. You do not control your settlements when you leave them. To collect taxes or use Pursuits, end your turn inside that Settlement. To Occupy a Settlement, begin a Battle adjacent to the city like a Siege — instead, you Battle against the Garrison and Armies at war with you or owned by the same owner. If you win (or there is no force to fight), move inside. In the Upkeep Phase, only pay upkeep on equipment. You count as having all Infrastructure of Occupied Settlements and always count as 3 Trading Pursuits. When you leave a Settlement, you may not re-enter it until you Occupy another Settlement and a Trade Agreement is signed.
The Wandering Crown

Wandering Nomads: Your armies function as settlements, classified as a Band, Tribe, or Horde and upgraded accordingly. You may have one additional army per Era, starting with two. Armies do not require troops to exist and cannot be besieged. Nomads cannot build infrastructure but may build pursuits. Raw Material pursuits within Reach are always considered active and do not take a settlement ward. Each army is considered to have a Muster Field. You may trade so long as your border touches another player's border. Armies count as settlements with a Reach of 3. When an army is destroyed, so is its settlement. You may begin a new army adjacent to any existing army by using either the Charter Settlement or Muster Army actions. Nomads do not pay any upkeep.
The Dukedom

The Great Arbiter: The Duke begins the game trading with all players under a Non-Aggression Pact. The Duke cannot join alliances, perform Cunning actions, or Declare War. If a player declares war on the Duke, that player's Trade Agreements, Non-Aggression Pacts, and Defensive Alliances are immediately and permanently voided. Their Military Alliance remains intact. All other players simultaneously declare war on that player and their Military Alliance. These cannot be reinstated while at war with the Duke. The Duke sees all private actions, resolves player actions, and manages Bandit Mechanics. If the Duke is eliminated, the game ends. The Duke may optionally choose a faction.
The Elder Grove
Wise & Suspicious: Gain Doubt +1; If Public Order is 1+, armies gain +1I, Steady, and Speed +1. Cannot be a member of an alliance.
The Yew Heart

Archery is a Way of Life: You begin the game with a Fletchery which does not occupy a Settlement ward, nor cost upkeep. You always gain its Mastery Effect, which cannot be deactivated. In addition, your armies must always be equipped with a ranged weapon. Ranged Weapons gain +1 to Strike. Cannot  be equipped with full plate or articulated gothic plate. Cannot use shields. Cannot build a Preceptory of Knight's Templar.
